nodes.definition: User can initiate a research session by entering a free-text research question.
nodes.label: Initiate Research Session

nodes.definition: System interprets the user's query and produces a structured research brief (research question, hypotheses, scope constraints).
nodes.label: Interprets User's Query

nodes.definition: System engages with the user to clarify an ambiguous query, asking targeted questions until the research brief is sufficiently specific.
nodes.label: Engages Clarify Ambiguous

nodes.definition: System generates multiple search query variants optimised for scholarly search APIs from the research brief.
nodes.label: Generates Multiple Search

nodes.definition: System retrieves paper metadata from scholarly sources using the generated queries.
nodes.label: Retrieves Paper Metadata

nodes.definition: System scores retrieved papers for relevance across multiple dimensions and produces a ranked list with accept/reject decisions based on configurable thresholds.
nodes.label: Scores Retrieved Papers

nodes.definition: User can specify preferred evidence types in the research brief, and the system factors those preferences into paper ranking.
nodes.label: Specify Preferred Evidence

nodes.definition: System tags each catalog entry with its evidence type for filtering and thematic grouping in the report.
nodes.label: Tags Each Catalog

nodes.definition: User can review borderline-scored papers and accept or reject them before download proceeds.
nodes.label: Review Borderline-scored Papers

nodes.definition: System downloads full-text content for accepted papers from available sources.
nodes.label: Downloads Full-text Content

nodes.definition: System extracts structured findings (claims, results, methodology, limitations) from downloaded papers into a research catalog.
nodes.label: Extracts Structured Findings

nodes.definition: System synthesises the research catalog into a structured report that directly addresses the original research question and hypotheses.
nodes.label: Synthesises Research Catalog

nodes.definition: System persists research session artifacts (motivation brief, queries, ranked papers, catalog) to disk for later review or resumption.
nodes.label: Persists Research Session

nodes.definition: User can list previously completed research sessions and open one for review.
nodes.label: List Previously Completed

nodes.definition: User can export the final research report as a PDF document.
nodes.label: Export Final Research

nodes.definition: User can export the complete research session (report + catalog + metadata) as an archive for sharing or backup.
nodes.label: Export Complete Research

nodes.definition: User can create, edit, and delete search queries before the search is executed.
nodes.label: Create

nodes.definition: User can manually upload PDF papers to a research session at any time (before, during, or after search), creating Paper entries in 'approved' status.
nodes.label: Manually Upload Pdf

nodes.definition: User can trigger catalog entry creation for an approved paper that has content but hasn't been processed yet.
nodes.label: Trigger Catalog Entry

nodes.definition: User can edit or redact extracted findings in a catalog entry to correct or refine the system's output.
nodes.label: Edit Redact Extracted

nodes.definition: User can import a list of papers from a citation management tool into a research session, producing Paper entries that the system ranks, downloads, and extracts into catalog entries.
nodes.label: Import List Papers

nodes.definition: System produces a sufficiency verdict after report synthesis - indicating whether the collected sources constitute an adequate review, and recommending action if not.
nodes.label: Produces Sufficiency Verdict

nodes.definition: System produces a structured hypothesis verdict in the report with a confidence assessment and links to supporting and contradicting sources.
nodes.label: Produces Structured Hypothesis

nodes.definition: User can select one or more catalog entries and trigger 'find similar sources' — the system analyses selected papers' key findings, tags, and title to generate new targeted search queries.
nodes.label: Select One More

nodes.definition: System generates citation network data (co-citation links between authors, citation links between papers) from the paper set for visualisation in the catalog view.
nodes.label: Generates Citation Network

nodes.definition: System groups catalog entries by thematic agreement and produces a consensus summary showing the number of supporting sources per finding cluster.
nodes.label: Groups Catalog Entries

nodes.definition: User can generate citations in standard formats (BibTeX, APA, MLA, Chicago) for one or more selected papers and export them as a bibliography file.
nodes.label: Generate Citations Standard

nodes.definition: User can filter and search papers within a session by metadata fields (title, author, date, keyword) to locate specific papers in the collection.
nodes.label: Filter Search Papers

nodes.definition: As a User, I want to start a session with my research question and receive a structured report answering it by the time the pipeline completes - including an evidence-type-tagged catalog, hypothesis verdict, and sufficiency assessment.
nodes.label: Start Research Question

nodes.definition: As a User, I want to upload my own PDFs, trigger catalog extraction on demand, and edit extracted findings during or after a search so that I can enrich the session with sources the system didn't find or get wrong.
nodes.label: Upload Pdfs

nodes.definition: As a User, I want to access and share my past research findings so that I can build on previous work and collaborate with others.
nodes.label: Access Share Past

nodes.definition: As a User, I want to import my curated paper lists from a citation management tool into a session so that the system can rank, download, and extract findings for them alongside discovered sources.
nodes.label: Import Curated Paper

nodes.definition: As a User, I want to see citation networks and findings agreement clusters in the catalog so that I can identify key authors, seminal papers, and areas of consensus or controversy at a glance.
nodes.label: See Citation Networks

nodes.definition: Percentage of completed sessions where the report directly addresses the research question and tests all stated hypotheses.
nodes.label: Percentage Completed Sessions

nodes.definition: Percentage of catalog entries containing at least main claim, key results, and study design (non-empty fields).
nodes.label: Percentage Catalog Entries

nodes.definition: Percentage of initiated sessions that reach report generation (not abandoned mid-pipeline).
nodes.label: Percentage Initiated Sessions

nodes.definition: Percentage of sessions where sufficiency check returns is_sufficient: true without needing rerun.
nodes.label: Percentage Sessions Sufficiency

nodes.definition: Percentage of sessions with a stated hypothesis that receive a non-null verdict in the report.
nodes.label: Percentage Sessions Stated

nodes.definition: Percentage of sessions where the clarification loop produces a research brief that the user confirms as accurate (user clicks 'proceed' without edits).
nodes.label: Percentage Sessions Clarification

nodes.definition: Percentage of generated search queries that return at least one paper metadata record from a scholarly source.
nodes.label: Percentage Generated Search

nodes.definition: Percentage of retrieved papers that receive a non-null relevance score and a valid accept/reject/threshold-band classification.
nodes.label: Percentage Retrieved Papers

nodes.definition: 100% of borderline-scored papers must be presented for accept/reject review before any download proceeds.
nodes.label: 100% Borderline-scored Papers

nodes.definition: Percentage of accepted papers where full-text is successfully downloaded or flagged for manual upload.
nodes.label: Percentage Accepted Papers

nodes.definition: 100% of catalog entries must be editable and redactable by the user after extraction completes.
nodes.label: 100% Catalog Entries

nodes.definition: Time in seconds to display filtered paper results after a metadata search query is submitted.
nodes.label: Time Seconds Display

nodes.definition: 100% of papers imported from a citation management tool must appear in the paper list with correct metadata (title, authors, date) within 60 seconds of import.
nodes.label: 100% Papers Imported

nodes.definition: 100% of completed sessions must be persisted to disk with all artifacts (brief, queries, papers, catalog) intact.
nodes.label: 100% Completed Sessions

nodes.definition: 100% of past sessions appear in the session list with correct metadata (title, date, status) when the list is displayed.
nodes.label: 100% Past Sessions

nodes.definition: 100% of query edits made before execution are saved and reflected in the next search batch.
nodes.label: 100% Query Edits

nodes.definition: Percentage of 'export as PDF' operations that produce a valid, readable PDF file with all report sections.
nodes.label: Percentage 'export Pdf'

nodes.definition: 100% of 'export full archive' operations produce an archive containing the report, catalog, and session metadata.
nodes.label: 100% 'export Full

nodes.definition: 100% of citation export operations produce a bibliography file in the user-selected format with all selected papers.
nodes.label: 100% Citation Export

nodes.definition: Percentage of 'find similar sources' results where the user accepts at least one suggested paper into the session.
nodes.label: Percentage 'find Similar

nodes.definition: 100% of catalog entries with at least one co-author or co-citation relationship are included in the citation graph visualization.
nodes.label: 100% Catalog Entries

nodes.definition: Percentage of catalog entries that are assigned to a thematic agreement group at synthesis time.
nodes.label: Percentage Catalog Entries

nodes.definition: A named research investigation, identified by `session_id`. Contains a motivation brief, search tags, queries, papers, catalog entries, and report. Persisted as a set of JSON artifacts on disk.
nodes.label: ResearchSession

nodes.definition: A term extracted from the research brief, carrying a context-specific `definition`, `synonyms` (feeds search tag generation), and `role` (construct, variable, method, outcome, or context).
nodes.label: KeyConcept

nodes.definition: A classification of terms derived from KeyConcepts. Three categories: primary_terms (strong relevance signal), supporting_terms (secondary signal), exclusion_terms (out-of-scope indicator). Also includes domain_tags, methodology_tags, and key_authors.
nodes.label: SearchTag

nodes.definition: A search string variant generated from SearchTags, carrying a formatted string, target endpoint, filters, execution order, and variant type classification (broad, narrow, methodological, author-focused, venue-focused, or temporal).
nodes.label: Query

nodes.definition: A campaign within a research session, grouping queries and their collected scholarly documents. Manages the lifecycle of query execution, result collection, and document acquisition.
nodes.label: Search

nodes.definition: Structured findings extracted from an approved scholarly work. Contains bibliographic data, relevance score, extraction confidence, research alignment (hypothesis support/contradiction + evidence type), findings (main claim, key results, conclusions, limitations, future work), methodology (study design, sample size, dataset, methods/tools), evidence (key metrics with values, direct quotes), and related DOIs.
nodes.label: CatalogEntry

nodes.definition: Classification of a scholarly work's contribution type: empirical quantitative, empirical qualitative, systematic review, meta-analysis, theoretical, case study, or mixed. Used for filtering, tagging, and thematic grouping.
nodes.label: EvidenceType

nodes.definition: The final synthesised output (defined by the output schema). Contains summary, hypothesis verdicts, and supporting evidence from catalog entries.
nodes.label: Report

nodes.definition: The report's assessment of the stated hypothesis: `supported`, `contradicted`, `mixed`, `insufficient_evidence`, or null (no hypothesis). Includes confidence score and supporting/contradicting DOI lists.
nodes.label: HypothesisVerdict

nodes.definition: Quality indicators on a structured finding when extraction is imperfect. Examples: short source, OCR noise, missing methods, paywall partial.
nodes.label: ExtractionFlag

nodes.definition: The human actor operating the Research Distillery system. Includes researchers, scholars, and graduate students conducting academic research.
nodes.label: User

nodes.definition: The automated Research Distillery application that processes research queries, manages pipelines, and produces reports.
nodes.label: System

nodes.definition: The system component responsible for creating, tracking, and persisting research sessions throughout their lifecycle.
nodes.label: Session Manager

nodes.definition: The system component that executes queries against scholarly search APIs and retrieves paper metadata.
nodes.label: Search Engine

nodes.definition: The system component that scores retrieved papers across multiple relevance dimensions and produces ranked lists with accept/reject decisions.
nodes.label: Ranking Engine

nodes.definition: The system component responsible for fetching full-text PDFs from open-access sources and Sci-Hub for accepted papers.
nodes.label: Downloader

nodes.definition: The system component that parses downloaded PDFs and extracts structured content for catalog entry generation.
nodes.label: Document Processor

nodes.definition: The system component that assembles the research catalog into a structured report with hypothesis verdicts and sufficiency assessments.
nodes.label: Report Synthesiser

nodes.definition: The system component that stores and retrieves all research session artifacts (briefs, queries, papers, catalogs, reports) on disk.
nodes.label: Persistence Layer

nodes.definition: The system component that generates co-citation and citation link data from the paper set for visualisation in the catalog view.
nodes.label: Citation Network Builder

nodes.definition: The system component that generates citation files in standard formats (BibTeX, APA, MLA, Chicago) for selected papers.
nodes.label: Citation Export

nodes.definition: The shared system component that intercepts failures across pipeline stages and presents actionable remediation options to the user.
nodes.label: Error Handling Middleware (Shared)

nodes.definition: Structured research brief derived from the user's free-text research question, containing hypotheses, scope constraints, and key concepts.
nodes.label: ResearchBrief

nodes.definition: A structured piece of information extracted from a paper, containing a statement, supporting evidence, and optional confidence score.
nodes.label: Finding

nodes.definition: An extracted assertion from a paper with supporting and contradicting evidence.
nodes.label: Claim

nodes.definition: A thematic grouping of catalog entries with a consensus summary showing supporting and contradicting source counts.
nodes.label: FindingCluster

nodes.definition: Citation network data containing co-citation links between authors and citation links between papers.
nodes.label: CitationNetwork

nodes.definition: A co-citation link between two authors, recording how many times they are cited together.
nodes.label: AuthorCoCitation

nodes.definition: Metadata for an exported research session archive, including format, path, and included papers.
nodes.label: ExportArchive

nodes.definition: A single clarification Q&A turn between user and system during research brief refinement.
nodes.label: ClarificationTurn

nodes.definition: A user edit or redaction to a catalog entry, recording the original and replaced values with timestamp.
nodes.label: UserEdit

nodes.definition: Possible outcomes for a hypothesis verdict: supported, contradicted, inconclusive, or not applicable.
nodes.label: VerdictOutcome

nodes.definition: Assessment of whether collected sources constitute an adequate review.
nodes.label: SufficiencyVerdict

nodes.definition: A scholarly document such as a paper, conference proceeding, preprint, or technical report. Identified by a unique identifier. May be retrieved via scholarly search APIs or imported from citation managers.
nodes.label: Source

nodes.definition: A logged system event recording a failure with context (session, source, failure code) and suggested recovery actions.
nodes.label: Error

nodes.definition: Lifecycle status of a source within a research session, from ranked through extracted or rejected.
nodes.label: SourceStatus

nodes.definition: An observational study where two groups are compared — one with the outcome of interest (cases) and one without (controls).
nodes.label: CASE_CONTROL

nodes.definition: A descriptive study tracking patients with a known exposure or treatment, without a control group.
nodes.label: CASE_SERIES

nodes.definition: A high-level study that identifies, appraises, and synthesizes all relevant studies on a research question.
nodes.label: SYSTEMATIC_REVIEW

nodes.definition: A study that observes a population at a single point in time to assess prevalence.
nodes.label: CROSS_SECTIONAL

nodes.definition: A study design that combines quantitative and qualitative research methods.
nodes.label: MIXED_METHODS

nodes.definition: Research conducted in a controlled environment outside a living organism (e.g., cell culture).
nodes.label: IN_VITRO

nodes.definition: Research conducted within a living organism (e.g., animal studies).
nodes.label: IN_VIVO

nodes.definition: A PDF source that contains many mathematical formulas, which may have extraction errors.
nodes.label: FORMULA_HEAVY

nodes.definition: A PDF that is a scanned image rather than text, potentially with poor OCR quality.
nodes.label: SCANNED_PDF

nodes.definition: A source written in a language other than English, which may have translation gaps.
nodes.label: NON_ENGLISH

nodes.definition: A verdict outcome indicating the hypothesis is not applicable to the collected evidence.
nodes.label: NOT_APPLICABLE

nodes.definition: A sufficiency verdict indicating more sources are needed to reach adequate coverage.
nodes.label: NEEDS_MORE

nodes.definition: A citation link between two authors, recording how many times they are cited together in the literature.
nodes.label: AuthorCitation

nodes.definition: A citation link between two scholarly sources, recording that one source cites another.
nodes.label: SourceCitation

nodes.definition: A lightweight metadata snapshot of a research session, including title, status, and references to its queries, papers, catalog entries, and report.
nodes.label: SessionSummary

nodes.definition: A single chat communication exchanged between the user and the system within a research session, carrying role (user/system), content, and timestamp.
nodes.label: Message

nodes.definition: A curated collection of scholarly sources organized by the user, containing multiple research sessions and their associated papers, findings, and reports.
nodes.label: Library

nodes.definition: Machine-readable error codes used to classify system failures, including network errors, parsing errors, download failures, rate limits, authentication failures, storage errors, validation errors, and unknown errors.
nodes.label: ErrorCode

nodes.definition: Error severity levels used to prioritise error handling and user notification.
nodes.label: ErrorSeverity

nodes.definition: Query execution lifecycle status, tracking a query from creation through execution to completion or failure.
nodes.label: QueryStatus

nodes.definition: Origin of a query: whether it was manually entered by the user, automatically generated from search tags, or derived from a similar source.
nodes.label: QuerySource

nodes.definition: Search campaign lifecycle status, tracking whether a search is currently running, has completed, or was cancelled.
nodes.label: SearchStatus

nodes.definition: Suggested recovery actions for a logged error event, providing actionable remediation options to the user.
nodes.label: ErrorRecovery

nodes.definition: Optional filter criteria used when querying research sessions, including status, text search, and library scope.
nodes.label: SessionFilter

nodes.definition: A testable statement about the expected relationship between variables, derived from the research question and refined through the clarification process.
nodes.label: Hypothesis

nodes.definition: The free-text question provided by the user that defines the scope and objective of the research session.
nodes.label: ResearchQuestion

nodes.definition: A numerical score computed by the ranking engine that indicates how well a paper matches the research question, used for accept/reject decisions.
nodes.label: RelevanceScore

nodes.definition: A formatted list of citations for selected papers, exported in standard academic formats such as BibTeX, APA, MLA, or Chicago.
nodes.label: Bibliography

nodes.definition: The complete persisted state of a research session including all artifacts, ensuring zero data loss after transient failures.
nodes.label: SessionState

nodes.definition: A citation management tool (e.g., Zotero, Mendeley) from which users can import paper lists into a research session.
nodes.label: CitationManager

nodes.definition: A temporary failure in the pipeline (e.g., network timeout, API rate limit) that may resolve on retry without user intervention.
nodes.label: TransientFailure

nodes.definition: The degree of agreement among catalog entries on a finding, measured by supporting versus contradicting source counts within a thematic cluster.
nodes.label: Consensus

nodes.definition: Bibliographic information about a scholarly source including title, authors, abstract, publication year, journal, and DOI, retrieved from search APIs.
nodes.label: SourceMetadata

nodes.definition: The user's explicit decision to include or exclude a borderline-scored paper from further processing.
nodes.label: AcceptRejectDecision

nodes.definition: A packaged export of a complete research session including report, catalog, and metadata, suitable for sharing or backup.
nodes.label: Archive

nodes.definition: The process of verifying the identity of a user or system component before granting access to resources.
nodes.label: Authentication

nodes.definition: The process of categorizing papers or findings into predefined categories or taxonomies.
nodes.label: Classification

nodes.definition: The unsupervised grouping of papers or findings based on similarity, used for thematic analysis.
nodes.label: Clustering

nodes.definition: A structured data store (relational or document-based) used for persistent storage of application data.
nodes.label: Database

nodes.definition: The process of extracting structured information (findings, claims, metadata) from unstructured PDF documents.
nodes.label: Extraction

nodes.definition: The process of selecting a subset of items based on specified criteria.
nodes.label: Filtering

nodes.definition: A significant word or phrase extracted from text, used for indexing and search.
nodes.label: Keyword

nodes.definition: The process of transferring data between storage systems, formats, or databases.
nodes.label: Migration

nodes.definition: Portable Document Format, a file format used for distributing documents, commonly used for scholarly papers.
nodes.label: PDF

nodes.definition: The process of analyzing a string of symbols (text or structured data) to determine its grammatical structure.
nodes.label: Parsing

nodes.definition: The process of ordering papers or results by relevance score or other criteria.
nodes.label: Ranking

nodes.definition: The act of attempting an operation again after a failure, often with exponential backoff.
nodes.label: Retry

nodes.definition: The process of assigning a numerical value to indicate quality, relevance, or confidence.
nodes.label: Scoring

nodes.definition: A blueprint or definition of the structure of data, including field names, types, and constraints.
nodes.label: Schema

nodes.definition: A specific release or iteration of a software component, document, or data model.
nodes.label: Version

nodes.term: Parallel Paths (feed into pipeline at any point)
nodes.label: Parallel Paths (feed into pipeline at any point)

nodes.definition: System must be implemented with a dynamically typed language suitable for data processing and a browser-based Web UI.
nodes.label: Must Implemented Dynamically

nodes.definition: All session artifacts must be stored as on-disk JSON files with raw PDFs — no database dependency.
nodes.label: All Session Artifacts

nodes.definition: The system must support PDF structural extraction with ≥90% completeness using Docling.
nodes.label: Support Pdf Structural

nodes.definition: The system must operate as a single-user, single-session application with no multi-tenant authentication.
nodes.label: Operate Single-user

nodes.definition: Each Paper must have a unique DOI within a session; papers without DOI are excluded from automated pipeline.
nodes.label: Each Paper Must

nodes.definition: Only one CatalogEntry may exist per Paper (1:1 relationship).
nodes.label: One Catalogentry Exist

nodes.definition: The system must handle Sci-Hub DNS failures gracefully with user prompts for manual upload.
nodes.label: Handle Sci-hub Dns

nodes.definition: All persisted JSON artifacts must carry a schema_version field with migration support.
nodes.label: All Persisted Json

nodes.definition: Once a report is generated, the pipeline is terminal; updates require explicit re-synthesis.
nodes.label: Report Generated

nodes.definition: Search execution must complete within ≤5 minutes per query variant across all endpoints.
nodes.label: Search Execution Must

nodes.definition: Paper scoring must complete within <10 seconds per batch.
nodes.label: Paper Scoring Must

nodes.definition: Storage budget must not exceed 200 MB per 30-paper session.
nodes.label: Storage Budget Must

nodes.definition: Session state must be preserved with 100% artifact integrity after transient failures.
nodes.label: Session State Must
